title: Dead Letter Channel

validation.research: Seven primary sources: Hohpe and Woolf’s Dead Letter Channel and Invalid Message Channel catalog entries; RabbitMQ Dead Letter Exchanges documentation; Amazon SQS dead-letter queue and redrive documentation; SQLite Transactions; and Python sqlite3 transaction/connection documentation. The established Dead Letter Channel name and DLQ/dead message queue aliases are explained. The original messaging-system undeliverability concern is distinguished from receiver-side invalid messages and modern product processing-failure facilities. Product-specific count, transfer safety, retention, ordering, and redrive transport-ID behavior are not generalized. The exact existing article was found and reused rather than duplicated.

runnable_example.verification: Exact demo output; 1/2 versus 3/1000 authoritative-failure-count boundaries; byte-exact original BLOB and complete expected failure metadata; unchanged retry state; reopening and already-parked status without rewriting evidence; full destination retaining source; forced error after failure insertion before deletion with full rollback; simultaneous same-receipt transfer once; two different receipts contending for one slot with no loss; abrupt subprocess exit between insertion and deletion; busy-BEGIN and failed-COMMIT propagation/rollback; invalid IDs/classification/counts/timestamps and missing-receipt handling without mutation; exact enqueue-time and signed-64-bit limits; 64/65-character receipt ID and 4096/4097-byte BLOB limits. No broker, handler, redrive, or power-loss guarantee is inferred.

example_limits: Revision of the existing Dead-Letter Queues article, preserving canonical ID data-dead-letter-queues, its original asset path, Data Engineering verse membership and tags, and the recovery/ownership perspective. No duplicate Dead Letter Channel article is created. Original bounded file-backed SQLite disposition simulation: trusted caller supplies a classified DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE failure count; fewer than 3 failures leave pending work untouched. At 3 or more, BEGIN IMMEDIATE coordinates an insert of original bytes/identity/timestamps/failure metadata and source deletion in one transaction. A one-record failure channel exposes capacity failure without losing the source. Receipt IDs are immutable and unique for the store lifetime; event IDs preserve business intent independently. Counts are 1..1000, source bodies are BLOBs up to 4096 bytes, and failure timestamps are nonnegative signed-64-bit integer milliseconds not preceding enqueue. Reopening recognizes already parked receipt IDs without rewriting evidence. This is not a handler, counter, scheduler, broker, remote handoff, redrive implementation, external-effect rollback, authentication, or power-loss test. Existing exact-pattern article is reused; primary collection moves to Messaging and Integration while its former Data Engineering collection retains a cross-reference.
